# Allotment season log

## March
Plots 1 to 12 dug over and manured from the compost bays. The bread co-op's
flour sacks made good weed suppressant under the paths. Early potatoes chitting
on the shed windowsill. Peregrine walked the site with the new tenants on
plots 7 and 11 and showed them the water butts and the tool library.

## April
Broad beans and peas sown direct. Onion sets in on plots 2, 3 and 9. A late
frost caught the first lettuces on plot 5; fleece is now in the shed for
everyone. The seed swap was the busiest yet, with forty people through the
hall. Slug pellets are banned on site; see the slug strategy note.

## May
Tomatoes and cucumbers into the greenhouse. Runner bean wigwams built on the
communal plot. Water butts full after a wet fortnight. The spring show
schedule was published, with a new class for the longest runner bean.

## June
First strawberries; surplus went to the bakery for their tarts. Blackfly on
the broad beans, dealt with by pinching out tips. The pond by the shed has
frogspawn turned to froglets, which may explain why the slugs are fewer.

## July
Heatwave. Watering rota extended to evenings. Two water butts ran dry; the
committee will look at buying two more. Courgettes in quantity; a box by the
gate for anyone to take. The quiet corner by the hedge was found trampled and
a polite notice put up.

## August
Main harvest. Plum glut from the old tree on the communal plot, shared with the
bakery for the frangipane. The show was a success: Brannoc's onions won their
class, and Isolde won the flower arrangement with dahlias and cosmos.

## September
Green manure sown on empty beds. Seeds saved from the best tomatoes for next
year's swap. Plot inspections done; two plots flagged for neglect with a
friendly letter first.

## October
Leaf collection for leaf mould begins, in the reused flour sacks. Garlic
planted. The greenhouse was emptied and washed down. The annual meeting agreed
the rent stays the same next year.

## Notes for next year
Order more fleece. Start the leaf mould earlier. Ask the bakery whether they can
spare more sacks. Consider a second compost bay for woody material only.
